newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices fought off profit-taking pressure to reach another six-year high at Saturday's close, but brokers expected the current liquidity-driven rally to show more caution ahead.

The weighted index ended 19.76 points or 0.24 percent higher at 8,182.44, surpassing the previous six-year high of 8,162.68 set on Friday and marking the highest finish since it reached 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$150 billion in Saturday's abbreviated session.
The market, fuelled by expectations of an extended economic recovery and abundant liquidity under the central bank's loose monetary policy, has gained more than 1,200 points or 19 percent in 1997.
"The more the market rises, the more selling pressue it will encounter," said Allen Huang, manager for National Securities.
"The market's uptrend is slowing, but it probably has some ways to go before falling into consolidation," he said.

Saturday's buyings focused on financials, which gained 0.91 percent as a sector with the "Big Three" commercial banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- rising T$4, T$4 and T$2 respectively to T$187, T$189 and T$147.
But industrial sectors dropped a collective 0.09 percent. Papers fell 1.45 percent on profit-taking while plastics lost 0.63 percent.
Brokers expected the market to continue seeing a small gain on Monday. A 8,150-8,250 range was seen.
